title: Plasma N-Glycoproteomics for BMI-discordant monozygotic twin pairs
projectDescription: The aim of the project was to identify altered plasma proteins and altered plasma N-glycopeptides from monozygotic twin pairs who are discordant for body weight. We performed targeted quantitative N-glycoproteomics from plasma samples from 48 twin pairs (n = 96 individuals).  This is the N-Glycopeptidomics part of the project. Proteomics of the same project has the accession number of PXD041384.
sampleProcessingProtocol: The samples were desalted using desalting plates and the buffer was changed to 25 mM Tris with 75 mM NaCl prior to sample processing. 70 ul of sample was passed twice through the plate and collected to new tubes. Next, albumin was depleted from the desalted samples. 50 ul of the desalted sample was incubated two minutes and passed through the resin. This was repeated once and after, three washes with 50ul wash buffer were collected with the flow-through. Bradford assay was used to measure the protein concentration of the samples and after this 440 ug of sample was aliquoted and dried. The dried samples were resuspended with 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate solution containing 0.2 % RapiGest denaturating surfactant and boiled for 10 minutes. The samples were reduced with 5mM final concentration of dithiothreitol (DTT) for 30 minutes in 60°C water bath and then alkylated with 15 mM final concentration of iodoacetamide (IAA) for 30 minutes. Reduced and alkylated proteins were digested using one µg sequence grade recombinant trypsin for every 100 µg of sample. The samples were incubated in 37°C and in darkness for 18 hours with the enzyme. After the digestion, the surfactant was made insoluble with an incubation for 45 minutes in 37°C with 0.5% end concentration of trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) which lowered the sample pH below two. The insoluble surfactant molecules were removed by centrifuging with 16,000 g in 8°C for 5 minutes. The leftover supernatant was dried and then resuspended in 55 µl 0.1% formic acid and. Size exclusion chromatography (SEC) was performed to separate glycopeptides and peptides. Prior to sample injection to SEC column, remaining aggregates were pelleted down with a centrifugation of 10,000 g in 18°C for 10 minutes and then 50 µl of the sample was injected to the SEC column. With a flow rate of 0.08 ml/min, fractions including minutes 13-19 (glycopeptides, 560 µl) and 20-31 (peptides, 960 µl) were collected. Column was washed for 30 minutes between the samples. 150 µl of peptide fraction and 135ul of glycopeptide fraction were dried. Peptide fraction was resuspended in 50 µl of 0.1% FA and 2% acetonitrile in water and peptide concentration was measured with peptide assay. Peptide samples were adjusted to 125 ng/ul and spiked in with internal Hi3 E.Coli standard in the final concentration of 50 fmol per injection in mass spectrometer. The dried glycopeptide samples were resuspended in 25 ul of 0,1% FA and 2% ACN in water without the internal standard for mass spectrometer.
dataProcessingProtocol: The mass spectrometer used in of the following procedures was a Synapt G2-Si equipped with a NanoAcquity UPLC (ultra performance liquid chromatograph). 1 ul of the glycopeptide mixture was applied to the trap column and injected to the Synapt. The method used to collect the quantitation data was MSE in sensitive and positive mode. Raw data was collected and uploaded to the Progenesis QIP and identified peptides were removed from the analysis. Statistically relevant N-glycopeptides with charges of three to five and m/z over 500 were picked for fragmentation. Fragmentation of the targeted N-glycopeptides was done with CID (collision induced dissociation) from the top three most abundant samples. Both MRM (multiple reaction monitoring) and wideband enhancement (singly and doubly charged fragments) with ion mobility fragment enhancement methods were used to all N-glycopeptide fragmentations. Peak lists were combined after. MascotDistiller was used to generate peak lists and the fragments and precursors were calibrated with a lock mass. Glycopeptide ID was used to identify the N-glycopeptides.
